newsitem.title: USA: Abbott, Roche AIDS drug mix stays potent.
newsitem.headline: Abbott, Roche AIDS drug mix stays potent.

text.p: A study has shown that a combination of two new drugs maintained its ability to drastically cut levels of HIV in infected patients after 12 weeks, Abbott Laboratories Inc and Hoffmann-La Roche said on Monday.
HIV viral load was reduced by 99.9 percent at 12 weeks with a combination of two protease inhibitors, Abbott Lab's Norvir Hoffmann-La Roche's Invirase, the companies said.
Hoffmann-La Roche is the drug unit of Roche Holding AG.

The data, presented at the 36th Interscience Conference on Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy, supports six-week data from the study released at the international AIDS conference in July. After six weeks, viral load was reduced by 99.6 percent by the combination of protease inhibitors.

"These data demonstrate not only the continued antiviral effect of this combination of two protease inhibitors but also the enhanced activity of the combination over time," said investigator Calvin J. Cohen of Community Research Initiative, New England, in a statement.

Protease inhibitors are the latest line of anti-HIV drugs that work by blocking an enzyme key to the virus's replication. Trials using the drugs in combination with older therapies, including Glaxo Wellcome Plc's AZT and 3TC, have also shown sharp drops in HIV levels.
The multi-center, open-label study of the two protease inhibitors randomized about 136 patients to one of four different treatment arms, the companies said.
The combined regimens were generally well-tolerated, with about seven percent of patients discontinuing, they said.
